title: Pakistan's 'Brotherhood With Muslim Cousins' Termed 'Disaster' For India: 'We're Not Going...' | Cricket News - News18
text: Pakistan’s show of solidarity with the Bangladesh cricket team could spell ‘disaster’ for India and the ICC, feels former England cricketer Mark Butcher, who says the raging controversy has its roots in the past when BCCI refused to send their team across the border for the Champions Trophy in 2025. The Pakistan government says its men’s cricket team won’t play their group-stage match of the 2026 T20 World Cup against India on February 15. No specific reason has been given, but it’s being seen as a protest against the ICC’s decision to replace Bangladesh with Scotland for refusing to travel to India for the tournament. Pakistan were the official hosts for last year’s Champions Trophy, but India played all their matches, including the semi-final and final, in the UAE after BCCI cited the government’s denial of permission to travel to the country. Butcher said Pakistan feel that Bangladesh haven’t been offered the same courtesy after they raised security concerns for not playing their World Cup matches in India. “Now Pakistan are in a situation, they are sort of a younger brother, or a cousin of India, and India pretty much gets its own way. It’s the most powerful and the wealthiest country in the world of cricket," Butcher said on Stick To Cricket podcast. “And therefore, Pakistan basically have to suck it up. So when they had the Champions Trophy in Pakistan, you could see it coming from a mile off that India were not going to go and play in Pakistan. So, everything got rearranged and this is where my biggest problem comes in. When this stuff happens, it affects all of the other teams in the tournament because all of a sudden, their programme has to change, they have to fly out of the country to go and meet India in a place they want to play and everybody else has to fit in." Butcher, who played 71 Tests between 1997 and 2004, says Pakistan’s “brotherhood" with Muslim cousins will be a financial disaster for India and the ICC. “They’ve (Pakistan) turned around and said, ‘Okay, we still want to be involved in the tournament. However, we are not going to play against India because of what you have done with Bangladesh. You had the opportunity to play our Champions Trophy that should have been in Pakistan and Dubai. You have not afforded Bangladesh the same courtesy. And therefore, in sort of a brotherhood with our Muslim cousins, we are not going to play against you.’ And for India, that’s a disaster. Or for the ICC, it’s a disaster because of the size, financially, of that fixture," he said. Butcher explained that the reason why India and Pakistan are always kept in the same group is because of the eyeballs it draws, which makes it the most lucrative fixture in the world of cricket. “The public in both countries, by and large actually, they are sort of brothers and sisters and they kind of get on fine. And the players between India and Pakistan have historically always gone fantastically as well. But above that, politically, not good, not a good look at all. So, bilaterally they don’t play against each other. However, in ICC tournaments, they are always placed in the same group. Why? Because it is the most lucrative fixture in the world of cricket. And some say in the world of sports," Butcher said. “So the ICC have to make sure that India and Pakistan are in the same group, and they are every single time. It’s not a coincidence that is done by rote from the top. Which is a bizarre situation, right? Other teams have to qualify, they get put in groups, it comes out of the hat, all the rest of it. But those two teams are always in the same group," he added. Pakistan have been warned by the ICC of punitive actions should they not take the field for their world cup match against India.

Pakistan were the official hosts for last year’s Champions Trophy, but India played all their matches, including the semi-final and final, in the UAE after BCCI cited the government’s denial of permission to travel to the country. Butcher said Pakistan feel that Bangladesh haven’t been offered the same courtesy after they raised security concerns for not playing their World Cup matches in India.
